A 40-year-old male seeks urgent care due to progressive fatigue over the past month, initially noticed
during hiking but now affecting daily activities. He has been medically unmonitored for over a decade,
with a history of untreated diabetes. His lifestyle includes poor dietary habits and moderate alcohol
consumption (1-2 beers daily), though he is a non-smoker. He has never undergone colonoscopy
screening. His vital signs show: temperature 99.3°F (37°C), blood pressure 155/66 mmHg, pulse
84/min, and respirations 20/min. Laboratory results reveal: - Hemoglobin: 8.9 g/dL - Mean corpuscular
volume: 70 fL - Ferritin: 400 ng/mL - TIBC: 200 micrograms/dL - Iron: 50 micrograms/dL What is the
most probable underlying cause of his symptoms? Answer Choices: (A) Alcohol-induced bone marrow
suppression (B) Myelodysplastic syndrome causing ineffective erythropoiesis (C) Hemoglobinopathy
such as alpha-thalassemia trait (D) Lead poisoning causing microcytic anemia (E) Occult bleeding (F)
Mineral deficiency (G) Erythropoietin deficiency due to chronic kidney disease (H) Iron malabsorption
due to celiac disease (I) Chronic inflammation (J) Vitamin deficiency
 A. Mineral deficiency
B. Iron malabsorption due to celiac disease
C. Hemoglobinopathy such as alpha-thalassemia trait
D. Vitamin deficiency
E. Myelodysplastic syndrome causing ineffective erythropoiesis
F. Chronic inflammation
G. Lead poisoning causing microcytic anemia
H. Occult bleeding
I. Erythropoietin deficiency due to chronic kidney disease
J. Alcohol-induced bone marrow suppression
